front_blocks.md: What is a hydrocarbon?

back_blocks.md: A hydrocarbon is a compound that contains **hydrogen** and **carbon** atoms only. It does not contain any other elements.

front_blocks.md: A displayed formula shows all the **..........** and all the **..........** in a molecule.

back_blocks.md: A displayed formula shows all the **atoms **and all the **bonds **in a molecule.

cards.front_md: A displayed formula shows all the **..........** and all the **..........** in a molecule.

front_blocks.md: What must be shown in a displayed formula that is not shown in a molecular formula?

back_blocks.md: A **displayed formula** shows the spatial arrangement of all atoms and all the bonds between them.
A molecular formula only shows the number and type of atoms, without indicating the bonds.

front_blocks.md: A student describes a hydrocarbon as a 'mixture of carbon and hydrogen molecules'. State two errors in this description.

back_blocks.md: Two errors:

1. Hydrocarbons are **compounds** (not mixtures)
2. They consist of carbon and hydrogen **atoms** (not molecules).
Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Carbon dioxide and metal carbonates are classified as organic compounds because they contain carbon.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

By convention, carbon dioxide and metal carbonates are **not classified as organic compounds**, even though they contain carbon. Organic compounds are carbon-containing compounds excluding these exceptions.

front_blocks.md: State three types of formula that can be used to represent organic compounds.

back_blocks.md: Organic compounds can be represented using:

- **Displayed formula** (showing all atoms and bonds)
- **Structural formula** (showing the arrangement of groups)
- **General formula** (showing the pattern common to a homologous series).

cards.front_md: State three types of formula that can be used to represent organic compounds.
cards.back_md:
Organic compounds can be represented using:

- **Displayed formula** (showing all atoms and bonds)
- **Structural formula** (showing the arrangement of groups)
- **General formula** (showing the pattern common to a homologous series).

front_blocks.md: What is a homologous series?

back_blocks.md: A homologous series is a family of similar compounds with similar chemical properties. Members share the same **general formula** and display a trend in physical properties.

cards.front_md: What is a homologous series?
cards.back_md: A homologous series is a family of similar compounds with similar chemical properties. Members share the same **general formula** and display a trend in physical properties.

front_blocks.md: Alkanes have the functional group **..........** , alkenes have the functional group **..........** , and alcohols have the functional group **..........** .

back_blocks.md: Alkanes have the functional group **C-C**, alkenes have the functional group **C=C**, and alcohols have the functional group **-OH**.

cards.front_md: Alkanes have the functional group **..........** , alkenes have the functional group **..........** , and alcohols have the functional group **..........** .
cards.back_md: Alkanes have the functional group **C-C**, alkenes have the functional group **C=C**, and alcohols have the functional group **-OH**.

front_blocks.md: How does the molecular formula change from one member to the next in a homologous series?

back_blocks.md: Each successive member of a homologous series differs from the previous one by one **CH**<sub>**2**</sub> unit. This means the molecular formula increases by one carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms.

cards.front_md: How does the molecular formula change from one member to the next in a homologous series?
cards.back_md: Each successive member of a homologous series differs from the previous one by one **CH**<sub>**2**</sub> unit. This means the molecular formula increases by one carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Members of the same homologous series have the same general formula and display a gradual trend in physical properties.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
All members of a homologous series share the same **general formula** and the same **functional group**. Physical properties such as boiling point change gradually from one member to the next.

front_blocks.md: Why do members of the same homologous series have similar chemical properties?

back_blocks.md: Members of the same homologous series have similar chemical properties because they all contain the same **functional group**, which is the part of the molecule responsible for the characteristic reactions of that series.

front_blocks.md: What is a saturated compound?

back_blocks.md: A saturated compound is a molecule in which all carbon-carbon bonds are **single bonds**. Alkanes are examples of saturated compounds.

cards.front_md: What is a saturated compound?

front_blocks.md: Unsaturated compounds contain one or more carbon-carbon **..........** bonds. **..........** are unsaturated compounds.

back_blocks.md: Unsaturated compounds contain one or more carbon-carbon **double **bonds. **Alkenes **are unsaturated compounds.

cards.front_md: Unsaturated compounds contain one or more carbon-carbon **..........** bonds. **..........** are unsaturated compounds.
cards.back_md: Unsaturated compounds contain one or more carbon-carbon **double **bonds. **Alkenes **are unsaturated compounds.

front_blocks.md: How can aqueous bromine be used to distinguish between a saturated and an unsaturated hydrocarbon?

back_blocks.md: When aqueous bromine is added, an unsaturated hydrocarbon (such as an alkene) **decolourises** the bromine water because it reacts via addition across the double bond. A saturated hydrocarbon (such as an alkane) does not react and the bromine water remains orange-brown.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
An alkane with four carbon atoms has the molecular formula C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub>.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

Alkanes follow the general formula C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>. With four carbons (n = 4), the formula is **C**<sub>**4**</sub>**H**<sub>**10**</sub>, not C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub>. C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub> is the formula for an alkene (butene).

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

cards.back_md:
**False.**

Alkanes follow the general formula C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>. With four carbons (n = 4), the formula is **C**<sub>**4**</sub>**H**<sub>**10**</sub>, not C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub>. C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub> is the formula for an alkene (butene).

front_blocks.md: Why are alkanes described as saturated while alkenes are described as unsaturated?

back_blocks.md: Alkanes are saturated because all their carbon-carbon bonds are **single bonds**, so no more hydrogen atoms can be added.
Alkenes are unsaturated because they contain at least one carbon-carbon **double bond**, allowing addition reactions to occur.

front_blocks.md: What does the stem of an organic compound's name indicate? For example, prop-.

back_blocks.md: The stem indicates the **number of carbon atoms** in the longest continuous carbon chain. For example, meth- = 1 carbon, eth- = 2 carbons, prop- = 3 carbons and but- = 4 carbons.

A compound with 4 carbons and only C-C single bonds is named **butane**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
But-1-ene and but-2-ene are the same compound, just named differently.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

But-1-ene and but-2-ene are **different compounds**. In but-1-ene the C=C double bond starts on the first carbon, while in but-2-ene it starts on the second carbon. The number indicates the position of the double bond.

front_blocks.md: Why is it necessary to include a number in the name but-1-ene but not in the name propene?

back_blocks.md: Propene has only one possible position for the C=C double bond, so no number is needed.
Butene has **two possible positions** (carbons 1 and 2), so a **number** is required to specify which carbon the double bond starts on.

front_blocks.md: Define **functional group**.

back_blocks.md: A **functional group** is the atom or group of atoms in an organic molecule that determines the compound's chemical properties and the family it belongs to.
For example, the –OH group is the functional group of alcohols.
